newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU stalls on rump Yugoslavia trade decision.
newsitem.headline: EU stalls on rump Yugoslavia trade decision.

text.p: The European Union decided on Monday to hold off giving rump Yugoslavia, which comprises Serbia and Montenegro, the preferential trade status granted to other countries in the region.

Diplomats said EU foreign ministers had agreed in principle to grant Serbia and Montenegro preferential trade treatment with the 15-country bloc -- but to delay implementation until at least their next meeting on December 6.

Problems related not only to the recent annulment of municipal election results but also to what the EU perceives as Belgrade's lack of assistance in pursuing alleged war criminals and continued tension over the Serb-governed Kosovo region, where many ethnic Albanians live.
"We felt it was a very unfortunate moment to do it right after the controversial elections," said a Dutch diplomat.
Serb authorities last Sunday annulled an opposition election victory in Belgrade, provoking renewed protest by opponents of the ruling Socialists and President Slobodan Milosevic.
Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, representing the EU presidency, met in the evening with Serbian Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic to discuss the issue.
"He expressed the concerns of the member states regarding the elections," an Irish official said.

Meanwhile, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind told reporters the purpose of next week's London conference on Bosnia would be to make clear to the country's formerly warring parties that military and humanitarian aid would not last forever.

"The single most important (item) is to press forward a degree of conditionality, to make it clear to the Bosnian people that continuation of economic and humanitarian help...is not unconditional, it's not open-ended," Rifkind told reporters.
